faqs.question: Is Friendsgiving before or after Halloween?
faqs.answer: In the US it comes after: Thanksgiving is Thursday 26 November 2026 and Thursday 25 November 2027, about 25 days after 31 October, so most Friendsgivings land in mid to late November. In Canada it comes before, because Thanksgiving falls on Monday 12 October 2026 and Monday 11 October 2027.

faqs.question: Can you have Friendsgiving in October?
faqs.answer: Yes. Canadian groups do it around the October long weekend anyway, and US groups whose members travel for Thanksgiving often move it into October so more people can come. An October Friendsgiving is also the simplest way to fold Halloween into the same night.

faqs.question: Is there a name for a party that mixes Halloween and Friendsgiving?
faqs.answer: There is no settled name; dictionaries record Friendsgiving but no blend with Halloween. Most groups invent their own label, and letting the group vote on one is a small way to make it a yearly tradition.

faqs.question: Do Friendsgiving guests have to wear costumes if it is near Halloween?
faqs.answer: No, and making costumes optional keeps the friends who dislike dressing up. A good middle rule is one costume piece, such as a hat or mask, that can come off when everyone sits down to eat.

faqs.question: What should the host cook at a potluck Friendsgiving?
faqs.answer: The host usually cooks the main course and lets guests cover sides, starters, desserts and drinks. For a group of 10, that means the host makes one dish and nine guests each bring one item from a shared list.

faqs.question: Is Galentine's Day only celebrated in February?
faqs.answer: The day itself is typically 13 February; it began as a 2010 Parks and Recreation episode about women's friendship. Borrowing its format for an October girls' night is a group's own invention, not a recognised second date.

faqs.question: How do I include friends who don't celebrate Halloween?
faqs.answer: Hold a plain Friendsgiving with no costume hour and no spooky décor, or invite them to the meal and let the costume part happen elsewhere. Some friends avoid Halloween on religious grounds, so check with them first.

faqs.question: How long should a Friendsgiving last?
faqs.answer: Three to four hours suits most groups: an hour of arrivals and starters, about 90 minutes at the table, then dessert. Setting an end time in the invite helps guests with early mornings say yes.

faqs.question: Can I send one SubhSandesh Halloween page to my whole friend group?
faqs.answer: Not as an invitation. Each Halloween page greets a single person and has a bestie mode, so they suit the friend who hosted or the friend who could not come, while the group plan belongs in your chat.

faqs.question: What date is Canadian Thanksgiving in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Monday 12 October 2026 and Monday 11 October 2027, the second Monday of October. That puts it 19 days before Halloween in 2026 and 20 days before in 2027.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Friendsgiving vs Halloween Party Ideas for a Friends-Only Night

Choosing between Friendsgiving vs Halloween party ideas comes down to how many free Saturdays your group really has. If it is one, merge them into a costume-optional potluck held between 31 October and US Thanksgiving, which sit 26 days apart in 2026 and 25 days apart in 2027. If it is two, keep the Halloween party loud and on its feet and the Friendsgiving seated and slow.

Lock the date early, because people leave occasions late. On SubhSandesh, 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were built on the festival day itself; that is a different festival and only 89 pages, used here as the nearest measured analogue. Whatever plan you send, 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, so keep it short enough to read on one screen. Below are the US and Canadian dates for 2026 and 2027, four tests for merging, potluck maths, six merged-night formats and a girls'-night Halloween.

## What is the difference between Friendsgiving and a Halloween party?

Friendsgiving is a Thanksgiving-style meal held by and for friends instead of family. [Wiktionary's entry for Friendsgiving](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Friendsgiving) describes it as a blend of "friends" and "Thanksgiving", popularised in the 2010s, with its earliest quotation from November 2011.

A Halloween party is a costume night tied to 31 October, eaten standing up. The real difference is the centre of gravity, a table versus a room people move through, and it sets your guest count, food plan and how hard the host works.

## The calendar: Halloween and Thanksgiving fall 19 to 26 days apart

Halloween is fixed: Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027. US Thanksgiving is the fourth Thursday of November, and the [US Office of Personnel Management holiday schedule](https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/) lists Thursday 26 November 2026 and Thursday 25 November 2027.

Canada's Thanksgiving comes first. The [Canada Revenue Agency's public holiday list](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/public-holidays.html) gives Monday 12 October 2026, and the second-Monday rule puts 2027 on Monday 11 October, 19 and 20 days before Halloween. These are the Saturdays that usually work:

- **US group, two events:** Halloween party Sat 31 Oct 2026 / Sat 30 Oct 2027; Friendsgiving Sat 21 Nov 2026 / Sat 20 Nov 2027.
- **Canadian group, two events:** Friendsgiving Sat 10 Oct 2026 / Sat 9 Oct 2027 on the long weekend; Halloween party Sat 31 Oct 2026 / Sat 30 Oct 2027.
- **US group, one merged night:** Sat 7 Nov 2026 / Sat 6 Nov 2027, while costumes are still out.
- **UK, India or Australia:** with no Thanksgiving holiday, one merged night is the easier sell.

## Should you combine them? Four tests and a 1912 idea

Émile Durkheim's *The Elementary Forms of the Religious Life* (1912; the 1915 Swain translation is [on Project Gutenberg](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/41360)) describes group life swinging between dispersion and concentration. Of moments of high feeling he writes: "Men look for each other and assemble together more than ever." A friend group runs on the same rhythm: ordinary scattered weeks, then a night that pulls everyone into one room.

A [2024 study in Royal Society Open Science](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11521598) paired 122 French adults into 61 pairs of strangers who watched amusing, sad or neutral videos side by side. Higher physiological arousal went with stronger mutual connectedness, but the link depended on the pair attending together, and the two did not need to feel the same emotion. It studied strangers and videos, not friends at dinner, so read it as a hint: one intense shared night may beat two lukewarm ones. Merge if two or more of these are true:

- Fewer than two Saturdays between 10 October and 21 November suit everyone.
- Half the group or more travels to family for Thanksgiving week.
- Only one person in the group is willing to host.
- A third or more of your friends dislike costumes but love a long dinner.

## Potluck or host-cooks: the numbers for 6 and 10 guests

Under six guests, the host can cook everything in one afternoon. From six up, a potluck spreads the cost and the oven time, and a shared list stops three people bringing dessert.

For a seated Friendsgiving of 10, give every guest exactly one job:

- 1 main course, cooked by the host
- 3 sides, one of them vegetarian
- 2 starters that can wait at room temperature
- 2 desserts
- 1 set of drinks, including one non-alcoholic option
- 1 run for ice, extra plates and takeaway tubs for leftovers

A Halloween party for the same 10 needs food eaten with one hand, since the other holds a drink or a prop. Ask about allergies in the invitation, not on the day.

## 6 ways to merge Friendsgiving and Halloween in one night

Each format gives what happens, who it suits, host prep time (an editorial estimate) and the guest's one job.

### 1. Costume hour, then the table

Guests arrive in costume for a standing first hour with snacks; at 8 pm the masks come off and everyone sits for the main course. It suits groups split between costume fans and dinner people. Host prep is about 3 hours; each guest brings one snack or one side.

### 2. Thanks-and-haunts round

Between main course and dessert, each person names one thing they are grateful for this year and one thing that genuinely scared them. It suits groups that have drifted a little. Host prep is 10 minutes to write the two prompts on a card; guests bring nothing but an answer.

### 3. The costume-recap Friendsgiving

On the merged Saturday after Halloween, everyone wears one piece of the costume they wore on 31 October and tells the story of the night it came from. It suits groups that scattered on the night. Host prep is a normal potluck; each guest brings a dish and the costume piece.

### 4. Three flats, three courses

Starters at one friend's place in full Halloween décor, the main at a second home set for Friendsgiving, dessert at a third. It suits friends living a short walk apart. Each host prepares one course for about 90 minutes; guests bring a coat and comfortable shoes.

### 5. The family-recipe table

Each friend brings one dish from their own family's holiday table, whether that is Thanksgiving, Diwali, Christmas or anything else, and says whose recipe it is. It suits international groups. Host prep is the main course only; guests bring the dish and its backstory.

### 6. Next year's date before dessert

Before anyone cuts the pie, the group picks next year's date and the next host, and one person saves it in a shared note. It suits every group that says "we should do this again". Host prep is zero; one guest volunteers as keeper of the note.

## A Galentine's-style Halloween night for 4 to 6 friends

[Galentine's Day, per Wiktionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Galentine%27s_Day), began as a 2010 *Parks and Recreation* episode and is now an informal day celebrating women's friendship, typically on 13 February. Searches for a "galentine halloween party" mostly return February pages, so here is an October version. "Girls' night" means whoever your group says it means; non-binary friends belong on the list if they belong in the chat.

- **6:30 pm:** a baked-potato bar. The host bakes; each friend brings one topping.
- **7:30 pm:** the compliment draw. Every name goes in a bowl, and you write one specific compliment for the friend you pull, then read it aloud.
- **8:15 pm:** one horror-comedy film, chosen by group vote a week before.
- **10:30 pm:** home. Ending on time is what makes people say yes next year.

## Friendsgiving vs Halloween party vs merged night, compared

Five formats, by date, food and dress code:

| Format | Best Saturday 2026 / 2027 | Food model | Dress code |
|---|---|---|---|
| Halloween party | 31 Oct / 30 Oct | One-hand snacks, potluck | Full costume |
| Friendsgiving (US) | 21 Nov / 20 Nov | Seated meal, 1 dish per guest | Smart-casual |
| Friendsgiving (Canada) | 10 Oct / 9 Oct | Seated meal, 1 dish per guest | Smart-casual |
| Merged night (US) | 7 Nov / 6 Nov | Costume hour, then seated meal | One costume piece |
| Galentine's-style Halloween | Any Saturday in October | Host bakes, guests bring toppings | Optional |

The merged night works because it borrows Friendsgiving's seated meal and keeps one piece of the costume party.

## Where SubhSandesh fits: one friend, not the guest list

Neither Halloween template is an invitation or RSVP tool; plan the party in your group chat. They are one-person greeting pages, right for the friend who hosted or the one who could not come.

The [interactive Halloween card with a bestie mode](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes: up to six photos, a letter, a pumpkin word, music, and the question "Will you be my boo-st friend forever?". Its No button runs away a few times, which a best friend will read as a joke. The [premium Halloween page with a voice note and unlock time](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes, holds a voice note of up to 60 seconds and up to 12 photos, and can stay locked until the hour you choose, such as the Friendsgiving toast. Its reply box takes one answer of up to 280 characters, emailed to you. 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect their page, worth doing if the letter names other friends. For a plain thank-you to the host after a non-Halloween dinner, [browse the full template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) instead.

## When to skip the merge, or the template

A merged night is the wrong call in four cases, and so is a template:

- **Friends who do not celebrate Halloween**, often for religious reasons: a straight Friendsgiving with no costume hour is the kinder default.
- **More than 12 guests:** a costume hour plus a seated meal outgrows most homes, so split it into two events.
- **A group that mostly travels at Thanksgiving:** a US Friendsgiving on 21 November 2026 may be half-empty, so move it into October.
- **A template for the whole group:** each page greets a single friend, in English, and cannot RSVP a crowd.

## Sources

- Wiktionary, "Friendsgiving" (earliest quotation November 2011).
- US Office of Personnel Management, Federal Holidays (2026 and 2027).
- Canada Revenue Agency, Public holidays 2026 (page dated 2026-01-06).
- Émile Durkheim, *The Elementary Forms of the Religious Life*, 1912; trans. J. W. Swain, 1915; Project Gutenberg eBook 41360.
- Chung, Mennella, Pacherie and Grèzes, "Social bonding through shared experiences: the role of emotional intensity", *Royal Society Open Science*, 30 October 2024.
- Wiktionary, "Galentine's Day".
